display.purpose: The pixel wordmark, once. Solid Lit Ivory over a wide gold glow.

lede.purpose: The one human sentence on the page. Two lines at desktop width is the budget.

label.purpose: The platform line under the command, and the only label voice left.

code-micro.purpose: The install command below 22rem. A deliberate floor for one breakpoint: a half-shown command reads as broken, so type size is what gets traded. Nothing else may use 9px.

readout.purpose: The specimen's measured labels. Tabular because the digits change every frame and must not shuffle sideways.

shadows.name: panel-lift
shadows.purpose: The install row only, and recorded as an outlier rather than doctrine. Depth in this system is emergence, not lift; do not propagate this to a second element.

shadows.name: wordmark-glow
shadows.purpose: Light, not shade. Makes the wordmark's pixel squares read as lit rather than printed.

shadows.name: readout-legibility
shadows.purpose: Functional only: keeps 9px mono readable over the specimen figure.

shadows.name: specimen-pool
shadows.purpose: A warm pool of light under the figure so it does not read as pasted on. The system's substitute for a shadow.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for every transition and entrance on the page.

motion.name: entrance
motion.purpose: opacity 0-1, translateY 14px-0, blur 7px-0. CSS keyframes by requirement, never JS: a content-hiding entrance must degrade to visible.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Hover and focus colour transitions on links and buttons.

motion.name: layer-crossfade
motion.purpose: The GL layer fading in over its server-rendered fallback, in the field (900ms) and the specimen (700ms).

motion.name: press-spring
motion.purpose: The copy button's press. Motion library, permitted because it moves something already visible.

motion.name: reveal-stagger
motion.purpose: The per-element --reveal-delay down the single column: portrait, wordmark, lede, install, icons.

motion.name: reticle-breath
motion.value: 5.5s alternate infinite, border-color 0.16-0.46 alpha, staggered negative delays
motion.purpose: The specimen's measurement boxes, so the plate reads as being actively read.

motion.name: sampling-cycle
motion.purpose: Each specimen region is mostly idle, then takes a pass. The five phases are offset so they never pulse in unison; the block size breathes on a second, slower period (t * 0.63).

motion.name: plate-reveal
motion.value: uReveal -0.16 -> 1.16 over ~1.1s, once, on first sight
motion.purpose: The wipe finishes above 1.0 because a window ending at exactly 1.0 closes again as the value passes it. The uniform defaults to 2 (fully open) so a loop that never runs leaves the plate visible.

components.name: Install Row
components.description: The page's primary call to action and the only lifted object in the system: a real, selectable shell command with a gold prompt and a text-button copy action.
components.html: $ curl -fsSL https://sfumato.sh/install.sh | sh
components.css: .ds-install-row { display: flex; align-items: stretch; width: 100%; max-width: 30rem; border: 1px solid rgba(203, 160, 83, 0.2); border-radius: 10px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(37, 31, 24, 0.72), rgba(11, 9, 8, 0.82)); backdrop-filter: blur(14px) saturate(120%); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(14px) saturate(120%); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(233, 225, 209, 0.05) inset, 0 18px 44px -22px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9); overflow: hidden; transition: border-color 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1); } .ds-install-row:hover { border-color: rgba(203, 160, 83, 0.34); } .ds-install-cmd { flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6em; padding: 0.85rem 0.5rem 0.85rem 1rem; font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.8125rem; color: var(--ivory, #e9e1d1); white-space: nowrap; overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none; } .ds-install-cmd::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; } .ds-install-prompt { color: var(--gold, #cba053); user-select: none; flex: none; } .ds-copy { flex: none; appearance: none; border: 0; border-left: 1px solid rgba(203, 160, 83, 0.18); margin: 0; padding: 0 1.1rem; background: transparent; color: var(--gold-dim, #a28757); font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1), background-color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1); } .ds-copy:hover { color: var(--gold, #cba053); background: rgba(203, 160, 83, 0.08); } .ds-copy:active { transform: scale(0.94); } .ds-copy:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gold, #cba053); outline-offset: -2px; }

components.name: Copy Button
components.description: The system's only button, and it is a text button: no fill, no icon, no toast. The label itself is the feedback (copy to copied, or select it when the clipboard is unavailable).
components.css: .ds-btn-copy { appearance: none; border: 0; border-left: 1px solid rgba(203, 160, 83, 0.18); margin: 0; padding: 0.85rem 1.1rem; background: transparent; color: var(--gold-dim, #a28757); font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1), background-color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1), transform 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1); } .ds-btn-copy:hover { color: var(--gold, #cba053); background: rgba(203, 160, 83, 0.08); } .ds-btn-copy:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gold, #cba053); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-btn-copy:active { transform: scale(0.94); }

components.name: Platform Line
components.description: The one mono label under the command. It replaced a four-line status paragraph: on a page whose whole argument is one command, that footnote was the largest block of text on screen.
components.css: .ds-platform-line { margin: 0.75rem 0 0; font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.6875rem; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8c8578; }

components.name: Icon Link
components.description: The whole navigation: three 44px hit areas holding 22px glyphs — source, docs, vitruvio. No visible text; the accessible name lives on the anchor.
components.css: .ds-link-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; } .ds-icon-link { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 44px; height: 44px; border-radius: 10px; color: #8c8578; transition: color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1), background-color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1); } .ds-icon-link:hover { color: #cba053; background: rgba(203, 160, 83, 0.08); } .ds-icon-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #cba053; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-icon-link svg { display: block; width: 22px; height: 22px; }

components.name: Specimen Plate
components.description: Salvator Mundi lifted off his ground and measured: five regions quantised in a shader, with DOM corner-tick reticles and real measured readouts over them. The first thing on the page and the only thing that moves on its own. The static markup below is the server-rendered layer; the GL canvas cross-fades over it and is what actually dissolves the crop.
components.css: .ds-specimen { margin: 0; width: min(clamp(200px, 28vw, 300px), 36vh); } .ds-specimen-stage { position: relative; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 820 / 912; background: radial-gradient(58% 46% at 50% 46%, rgba(148, 103, 18, 0.16), transparent 72%); } .ds-specimen-base { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: contain; -webkit-mask-image: radial-gradient(84% 66% at 50% 40%, #000 52%, transparent 100%); mask-image: radial-gradient(84% 66% at 50% 40%, #000 52%, transparent 100%); } .ds-specimen-marks { position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; } .ds-reticle { position: absolute; border: 1px solid rgba(233, 225, 209, 0.34); animation: ds-reticle 5.5s cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1) infinite alternate; } .ds-reticle:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: -1.9s; } @keyframes ds-reticle { from { border-color: rgba(233, 225, 209, 0.16); } to { border-color: rgba(233, 225, 209, 0.46); } } .ds-reticle::before, .ds-reticle::after { content: ""; position: absolute; width: 5px; height: 5px; border: 1px solid #cba053; opacity: 0.55; } .ds-reticle::before { top: -1px; left: -1px; border-right: 0; border-bottom: 0; } .ds-reticle::after { right: -1px; bottom: -1px; border-left: 0; border-top: 0; } .ds-readout { position: absolute; left: 0; bottom: calc(100% + 3px); display: flex; gap: 0.5em; align-items: baseline; white-space: nowrap; font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.5625rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #b9b2a0; text-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(8, 7, 6, 0.9); } .ds-readout-block { color: #a28757; }

components.name: Wordmark
components.description: The name, in Geist Pixel Square, sitting into the dissolved base of the specimen. Solid Lit Ivory with a wide gold glow — light, never a clipped gradient.
components.css: .ds-wordmark { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-pixel, ui-monospace, monospace); font-weight: 400; font-size: clamp(2.75rem, 9vw, 8.25rem); line-height: 0.86; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: var(--ivory, #e9e1d1); filter: drop-shadow(0 0 26px rgba(203, 160, 83, 0.22)); }

narrative.overview:
A five-century-old painting surfaces out of the dark, the name sits into its base, and under it there is exactly one thing to do. The page is a single centred column that fits in a viewport: the measured plate, the wordmark, one line of language, the install command, three icons. Nothing scrolls and nothing enumerates features — a visitor who has read the line either runs the command or follows a link, and everything that was neither of those has been removed.

The register is warm, varnished and tonally continuous: things emerge from near-black rather than sitting on it. Salvator Mundi carries the identity, and he carries it *as a specimen* — the page samples five regions of the painting and reports what it measures there, in mono, at 9px. That is the tension the whole system runs on: the painting is tonally continuous, the instrument reading it is gridded and unhurried, and the product's name is what happens between them. The plate is the only place the page still speaks in that machine voice at any volume; the command and the platform line are the quiet end of it.

Nothing here is decided by taste where it could be decided by measurement. The palette is sampled from the three source paintings by k-means in CIELab, not eyeballed from them — which is why ochre-gold rather than any brand hue is the accent. The specimen's readouts are computed from the actual pixels underneath them: μ is mean luminance and ∇ is mean gradient magnitude, which is literally how gradually tone moves — the quantity sfumato is named for. The vitruvian glyph in the link row was drawn against the original at 20, 28, 64 and 140px and reduced to the parts that survive at icon size. That provenance is load-bearing: a contributor who substitutes a plausible-looking value for a measured one has broken the system even if it looks identical.
keyCharacteristics: One screen, one action; no sections, no scroll, no feature list.
Warm near-black ground (`#0b0908`), never neutral grey and never cool.
One accent hue, ochre-gold, sampled from the Baptism's halos.
Three type faces, one job each, and only one sentence of language.
Depth by emergence — atmosphere, masks and light pools, not shadows.
Imagery has no edge: every plate and the specimen dissolve to zero alpha.
Every number on screen is measured, or it is not on screen.

rules.name: The Rationed Light Rule
rules.body: Gold is light, not paint. It appears as thin strokes, small marks and single glyphs — never as a filled button, badge, panel or block. If a gold region is large enough to read as a shape, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Warm Ground Rule
rules.body: Every dark value has more red than blue. There is no neutral grey and no cool black anywhere in the palette. A `#0a0a0a` or a `slate-950` is an immediate identity break, however subtle it looks alone.

rules.name: The Three-Tier Text Rule
rules.body: Language descends through exactly three ivories — Lit for the name and the command, Veiled for the sentence, Muted for chrome. Reaching for an opacity on ivory instead of the next tier down fragments the ramp. There is no fourth tier: the page no longer has anything quiet enough to need one.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Pixel is identity. Mono is machine surfaces. Sans is the one human sentence. No face ever takes another's job — Sans never becomes chrome, Mono never sets prose, Pixel never appears outside the wordmark.

rules.name: The Cell Rule
rules.body: Every Pixel size is an exact multiple of the 11px mono cell. The pixel grid and the mono grid never drift out of step, which is why they read as one system rather than two fonts.

rules.name: The Pixel Echo Rule
rules.body: Pixel-grid forms appear three times and always as identity: the wordmark, the favicon's S, and the same S as the docs icon in the link row. Used once, a pixel form reads as a lone exotic; those three are what make it structural. Do not add a fourth occurrence for decoration, and do not let the three drift apart — they are the same letter drawn on the same grid.

rules.name: The Single Label Voice Rule
rules.body: Any mono *label* shares one size, one case and `0.16em` tracking. A label at a different size is a new voice, and there is no budget for one. The readout is not an exception to this: it is not a label, it is a number the machine took off the painting, and its tracking, size and tabular figures all follow from that.

rules.name: The One Screen Rule
rules.body: Everything on this page fits one viewport at 1280×720 and at 390×844. Anything that would introduce a scroll belongs on `docs.sfumato.sh`.

rules.name: The No Panels Rule
rules.body: Nothing is separated by a surface. There is no card, no section background and no divider rule on this page — the centring and the gaps do all of it.

rules.name: The Emergence Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from masks, screen blending, gradients and light pools — never from `box-shadow`. If a new element needs to feel raised, give it light or give it space.

rules.name: The No Edges Rule
rules.body: Imagery in this system has no boundary, and **alpha alone cannot remove a crop**. The bust is a cutout, but the subject runs off the frame on three sides — the chest is sliced flat at the foot, the arm and the hair at the flanks — so its alpha is fully opaque right up to the border and it reads as a rectangle sitting in the page. Removing that is a per-pixel job, and it belongs to the shader (mechanism 4 above), not to a mask on a wrapper.

rules.name: The One Edge Rule
rules.body: When something needs marking off, mark one side — a border, a top rule, or two opposing corner ticks.

rules.name: The Visible-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Any animation whose start state hides content must be authored in CSS. JavaScript may only move, colour, or spring things that are already visible.

dos: **Do** keep the page to one screen and one action. New material goes to the docs.
**Do** keep every dark value warmer than neutral — more red than blue, in the `#080706` / `#0b0908` / `#12100d` family.
**Do** ration Halo Gold to thin strokes, small marks and single glyphs. If a gold region reads as a shape, reduce it.
**Do** size every Pixel occurrence as an exact multiple of the `0.6875rem` cell, and keep the three pixel forms (wordmark, favicon, docs icon) the same letter.
**Do** dissolve an image's crop per-pixel in the shader, and mask the fallback `` itself rather than the box that holds its instrumentation.
**Do** produce depth with masks, screen blending, gradients and pools of light.
**Do** author any content-hiding entrance as CSS keyframes with `animation-fill-mode: both`.
**Do** ship a server-rendered fallback beneath every GL layer, default its uniforms to the *open* state, and freeze motion under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** stop every animation loop off-screen and on hidden tabs.
**Do** measure any number that appears on screen from the pixels actually underneath it, and set changing digits in `tabular-nums`.
**Do** draw a new icon against the real thing at 20, 28, 64 and 140px, and cut whatever stops reading at the smallest size.
donts: **Don't** add a section, a feature list, a testimonial row or a footer. The page has one screen; the argument for a second one is an argument for a docs page.

**Don't** import generic dark-SaaS chrome: no violet or blue gradient buttons, no glass cards in rows, no neon borders, no purple-on-black. A cool accent destroys the warm-earth identity instantly, and this palette was sampled rather than chosen — it is not a preference to be traded.
**Don't** add a fourth type voice, and don't let an existing face take another's job.
**Don't** present the paintings as framed imagery — no bordered image, card, carousel, lightbox or museum caption. Any visible rectangular image edge is a defect.
**Don't** raise the background's Salvator or Baptism plates back to full strength; the specimen is the same painting and the icons sit over the Baptism's glow.
**Don't** mask the `.portrait` wrapper. The readouts live inside it, and a fade across the frame takes the lowest one with it — see the No Edges Rule.
**Don't** size the plate on width alone; its aspect makes it the tallest thing in the column and it will push the icon row off a laptop screen.
**Don't** invent numbers. No fabricated metrics, confidence scores or decorative readouts. If a value appears on screen it is measured.
**Don't** clip a gradient into text, on the wordmark or anywhere else. Gold is light; emphasis comes from size, weight and the glow.
**Don't** let the sentence under the name grow past two lines at desktop width.
**Don't** use `box-shadow` to raise an element. The install row's lift is a recorded outlier, not a precedent.
**Don't** wrap a region in a background, card or panel to separate it.
**Don't** drive an entrance from JavaScript, and don't use `motion` for anything whose start state is `opacity: 0`.
**Don't** caption a flourish. If a conceit needs a legend to land, it is a lecture.
**Don't** put a label above the wordmark to introduce it. That slot has been filled with decoration every time it existed.
